grammar_concept.title: Absolute Constructions
grammar_concept.rule: An absolute construction is a phrase, often with its own implied subject and a participle (-ing or -ed) or 'with/without', that adds background information, a condition, or a reason to a sentence without a linking conjunction like 'because' or 'if'. It stands grammatically apart from the main clause, connected only by a comma.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: This goes further than the participle clauses taught at B2 (where the subject of the participle is the same as the main clause's subject): here, the participle phrase can have its OWN subject, different from the main clause — 'Weather permitting, we'll go' means 'IF the weather permits', even though 'we' is the subject of 'go', not of 'permitting'. It's a compact, formal way to pack in a condition, reason or circumstance.
grammar_concept.example: Weather permitting, the ceremony will take place outdoors. All things considered, the project was a success. With prices rising, many families are cutting back on spending.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Se o tempo permitir, a cerimónia vai realizar-se ao ar livre. Considerando tudo, o projeto foi um sucesso. Com os preços a subir, muitas famílias estão a cortar nos gastos.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português tende a preferir uma oração completa com conjunção ("se o tempo permitir", "considerando que") em vez desta forma compacta sem conjunção — falantes de português muitas vezes inserem "if"/"because" mesmo quando a estrutura absoluta já os torna desnecessários ("If weather permitting, we'll go"), o que é redundante/incorreto.
grammar_concept.correction: Numa construção absoluta, não se usa conjunção antes do particípio — a própria estrutura (substantivo/pronome + particípio, ou "with/without" + substantivo) já indica a relação de condição/razão/circunstância, sem "if"/"because".
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In a formal announcement: "All things considered, the board has decided to proceed with the merger."

example_sentences: Weather permitting, the flight will leave on time.

vocabulary.definition_en: the joining of two or more companies into one
example_sentences: The merger was approved by both boards.
The plan will go ahead, provided that funding is approved.

exercises.prompt: Complete: ___ permitting, the ceremony will take place outdoors.
exercises.explanation: "Weather permitting" é uma construção absoluta fixa — sem conjunção antes.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Acrescentar "if" antes ("If weather permitting") é redundante — a estrutura absoluta já contém a ideia condicional.

exercises.prompt: Complete: All things ___, the project was a success.
exercises.explanation: "All things considered" usa o particípio passado ("considered") — o sujeito implícito é "tudo", que É considerado (voz passiva implícita).
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "considering" (particípio presente) inverteria o sentido — sugeriria que "tudo" está a considerar algo, não a ser considerado.

correct_answer: the joining of two or more companies into one
exercises.explanation: "Merger" significa a fusão de duas ou mais empresas numa só.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What condition does the speaker mention?
exercises.explanation: No áudio: "The plan will go ahead, provided that funding is approved by the board next week."
exercises.transcript: The plan will go ahead, provided that funding is approved by the board next week.

exercises.prompt: Read: "With prices rising sharply, many families are cutting back on non-essential spending." Why are families cutting back?
distractors: because they are saving for a holiday
exercises.explanation: "With prices rising sharply" é a construção absoluta que dá a razão — equivale a "because prices are rising sharply".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (usando uma construção absoluta): "Considerando tudo, a fusão foi um sucesso."
correct_answer: All things considered, the merger was a success.
exercises.explanation: "All things considered" é a construção absoluta fixa correspondente a "considerando tudo".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir literalmente como "Considering everything" não está errado, mas "all things considered" é a expressão idiomática fixa mais natural em registo formal.

steps.content: Absolute constructions are typically set off with a brief pause (reflected by the comma) — "Weather permitting, [pause] we'll go" — the pause signals that a self-contained condition or circumstance has just been added, before the main clause continues.

steps.prompt: Use an absolute construction to add a condition or reason to a plan you have — e.g. 'Weather permitting,...' or 'All things considered,...'.
Write 3 formal sentences using different absolute constructions (weather permitting, all things considered, with + noun + -ing).
